INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – SEPTEMBER 18, 2019

The Inglewood Library Board met on September 18, 2019 at the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall. The
meeting was called to order at 6:32 p.m. by Vice Chairman Julie Minton.

Roll Call

Present:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Staff:
  Harjinder Singh – Deputy to the City Manager
  Sabrina Barnes – Parks, Recreation and Community Services Director
  Frances Tracht – Library Manager
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Absent Staff:
  Brenda Davis – Management Assistant

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Minton made a motion for the approval of the minutes for August 28, 2019; Board
Member Castillo seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Minton, Castillo, Douglas and Cochran
  Nays: None

Library Report

  Sabrina Barnes introduced Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh, who worked on the
Inglewood Senior Center Project, to give a verbal report on the plan of the Main Library improvement
project. Mr. Singh introduced himself and spoke about his 17 years of experience working with the City in
different departments and with the Senior Center Project. Mr. Singh also spoke about the process and
timelines for the Main Library’s renovation project. Right now they are putting together a request for
qualifications to hire an architect who will combine with a construction manager and a library subject matter
expert. They will work as a team to create the design criteria. After this is completed, they can start pricing
the project and hire a design/build company to make the plan come to life.

  1
 Friends Report

  Susan Carleo, President, Friends of Inglewood Public Library, talked about very successful book
sale on September 14, 2019 and thanked Councilman Franklin from District 4 and Councilman Padilla from
District 2 for their outreach, support and purchases at the book sale. Carleo mentioned about the amazing
assortment of books that we get donated by our community that is really fits with our community and about
constant flow of new and fresh materials for people to purchase. Carleo also announced the Winter Book
Sale that will held on Saturday, December 14, 2019, 10:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m. Board member Castillo thanked
everyone for doing a good job. He bought a book and was very happy. Board member Sanders asked if
she can donate DVDs. Carleo answered yes and thanked everyone.

Public Comments

  Gregory Mason asked when the City will hire a Library Director. He was not happy about signs on
Manchester, Century and other streets in the area, about gentrification and canceled Library Board
Meetings. Board member Minton explained the rules of having board meetings and the reasons for
canceled meetings.
  Susan Janson asked about becoming a member of Friends of Inglewood Public Library,
complained about not having meetings and talked about her ideas:
   To create a small nook someplace in the library with the screen, to show the winning
  categorize books to show what's being considered or what worthy.
   Having poetry workshops and poetry events, have a poetry slam for the youth, in
  conjunction with the local schools, have some musical poetry, make it to a social event and
  a young professional Marcus Omari is interested in working with literacy.
   There is a grant available from The Romance Writers of America that could sponsor an
  area of the library to make a little romantic nook with lots of books, have some red roses
  from the ceiling, artificial intelligence to make a little magic for romance books.
   Have some of the players from sports teams to come encourage and show children many
  ways of advancement.
   Our librarians need to be more involved in what type of books we receive from Brodart and
  not just get what they want to sell us.

Commissioner Comments

  All Board Members were very pleased and excited with the plan.
  Board member Castillo also thanked Mr. Singh for doing a great job with the Senior Center project.
  Board Member Sanders talked about Library being a jewel of the city, thanked everyone for doing a
great job and that city also need to look back into the Library employee salaries, make it more comparable
with the great job that they do. She also talked about the library as a voting place.

  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 7:41 p.m.
